claims.text: Introducing a uniform nanoscale Y2O3 dispersion into tungsten enhances dynamic recovery during high-temperature deformation.
Y2O3-mediated dynamic recovery delays the onset of plastic strain in tungsten.
A uniform nanoscale Y2O3 dispersion increases the high-temperature toughness of tungsten.
Mechanical alloying with Y2O3 followed by high-temperature sintering can produce a fine, uniform, and stable oxide dispersion in tungsten.
Temperatures of 1200–1400 °C in inert or vacuum atmospheres are representative conditions for the proposed fusion plasma-facing comparison.
Spatially distributed Y2O3 nanoparticles act as pinning points in the tungsten matrix.
Spatially distributed Y2O3 nanoparticles act as vacancy sinks in the tungsten matrix.
Y2O3 particles impede dislocation motion by acting as localized obstacles.
Y2O3 particles enhance vacancy consumption and thereby accelerate dislocation annihilation.
Obstacle pinning and accelerated dislocation annihilation slow the accumulation of dislocation density.
Slower dislocation-density accumulation delays plastic yield.
A uniform Y2O3 dispersion inhibits localized dislocation pile-up.
Reduced dislocation pile-up contributes to increased high-temperature toughness.
Y2O3-dispersed tungsten will have a lower high-temperature plastic strain rate and a later onset of plastic deformation than unalloyed tungsten.
Y2O3-dispersed tungsten will develop a lower early-stage dislocation density than unalloyed tungsten.
Y2O3-dispersed tungsten will exhibit greater energy to failure and delayed crack initiation during cyclic and creep loading.
The proposed effects should persist only while the oxide dispersion remains uniform and stable during prolonged high-temperature exposure.
Dispersion inhomogeneities may create local stress concentrations that alter the proposed behavior.
